model.statement: The operator's "이 섹션 필요 없으니까 삭제" is recorded as a DISABLE of a PageRegion id. The Recon Template is never mutated; the disable becomes physical only in the BUILD COPY of the app, at the same point in the bake where bakeContent / bakeSeoTitles / bakeBrand already mutate that copy.
model.authoredField: authored.disabledRegions?: Record<regionId, { scope: 'global'|'routes', routes?: string[], reason?, note?, updatedAt }>
model.separateFromRoutes: authored.disabledRoutes and authored.disabledRegions are TWO optional fields, never one mixed map: they stale different stages, are refused for different reasons, and one map could not express 'this region is off everywhere' and 'this page is off' without one of them lying.
model.absentWhenEmpty: Both fields are optional and DELETED when their last entry goes, following the authored.assets / authored.brand precedent exactly (src/release/types.ts AuthoredStateSchema is .strict() and hashAuthoredState hashes the snapshot as captured, so a required-but-empty map would change the hash of every historical authored state and manufacture a spurious revision on the next prepare). Proven by smoke:enablement 28.P5.1 / 28.P5.4 / 28.P5.9.
model.noDerivationEvidenceStored: A disabled-region record stores NO node ids, slot keys, page ids or interaction facts. Everything is re-derived from the artifacts on every resolve, so a template recompile that moved an id is CAUGHT rather than applied blind (smoke:enablement 28.P5.12 refuses an extra `nodeIds` key; smoke:release 28.P5.68 proves a stale id disables nothing and is refused at resolve time).
model.writeApi: src/release/authored.ts — setAuthoredRegionDisabled / removeAuthoredRegionDisabled plus the `disable-region` / `enable-region` AuthoredEdit ops. Every function reports whether anything changed; a route list is deduped and sorted before comparison so re-issuing the same decision in a different order is a NO-OP (28.P5.6, 28.P5.7).
model.resolution: src/release/enablement.ts `resolveEnablement(authored, inputs)` → { plan, refusals, regionEffects, route, disabledSlots, warnings }. It is re-run and re-SAFETY-CHECKED on every build (build.ts memoizes it per build), never trusted because an edit was once accepted.
model.application: src/production/enablement.ts `applyEnablementToApp(appDir, plan)` removes the region ROOT node (and with it the whole subtree) from the build copy's page trees. A render-time 'hidden' flag was rejected: it would leave the markup in the shipped bytes, where the bake's own source-brand census still counts it and 'view source' contradicts what the operator was told.

safetyRules.rule: A region's ROUTE BLAST RADIUS is region.pages[].routes (RegionPageSchema: 'Many routes -> one pageSourceId. Never collapsed to the first one.'). It is NOT slot.route (the recon-template grouping records the FIRST route serving a page) and it is NOT derivable from the regionId, which is namespaced by pageSourceId and cannot name a route at all. A request naming a STRICT SUBSET of the radius is REFUSED with code `shared-page-blast-radius`.
safetyRules.realCounterexample: data/stripe.com/recon-templates/2026-08-18T10-45-40-007Z + page-regions/2026-08-26T16-14-08-675Z. MEASURED: 20 routes over 18 pages, 2 MANY-TO-ONE groups (p000012 <- 2 routes, p000013 <- 2 routes). The chosen region p000012:rgn:doc:div:1>div:1>section:2>div:1>div:2>div:1>div:1>div:2>article:1 carries 109 slot keys and renders on /resources/more/arr-loans-explained AND /resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained.
safetyRules.refusedBranch: scope 'routes' naming only /resources/more/arr-loans-explained -> allowed=false, refusal.detail.wouldAlsoAffect = ['/resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained'], cascadeAvailable=false, and the message states the reason (the id is namespaced by pageSourceId). smoke:enablement 28.P5.56 / 28.P5.57 / 28.P5.58.
safetyRules.safeBranch: scope 'global' on the same region -> allowed=true, effect.blastRadius names BOTH routes, effect.pageSourceIds is exactly ['p000012'] and every removed occurrence is on p000012 — no phantom per-route copy. smoke:enablement 28.P5.59 / 28.P5.60.
safetyRules.alsoRefused: Naming a route the region does not render on is refused as `route-not-in-region-radius` (28.P5.61) — a no-op recorded as a decision is still a lie.

safetyRules.rule: A region is GLOBAL FOR ENABLEMENT when ANY of three signals fires (the widest answer, never the narrowest): (i) region.scope === 'global' (the compiler's strict lift); (ii) a member slot key whose slots.json scope is `global`; (iii) the region's (landmarkKey, childPath) signature occurring on >= 2 distinct pageSourceIds. Such a region may ONLY be disabled with scope 'global' — `scope: "routes"` reads as 'for these routes and not the others', which cannot be true of it whatever route list accompanies it.
safetyRules.whyNotTheCompiler: REGION_COMPILER_VERSION exists because a selection-policy change MOVES EVERY ID, and an authored decision keyed on a moved id addresses nothing. The compiler, its policy and its ids are untouched.
safetyRules.realCounterexample: linear.app 2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z + page-regions 2026-08-26T16-14-07-901Z. MEASURED: the compiler's strict lift finds 5 global regions of 68; the three-signal union finds 25. All EIGHT page-scoped `footer1:self` regions are recovered by signal (ii) — each carries the identical 84 `global.footer.*` slot keys, and only a single element-count difference on /changelog keeps them page-scoped for the compiler.
safetyRules.measuredSlotSharing: 134 of linear's 3,079 slot keys belong to more than one region, and the 84 `global.footer.*` keys are each owned by ALL EIGHT footer regions (smoke:enablement 28.P5.28 / 28.P5.28b). region-plan.ts maps a slotKey to its FIRST owning region, which would under-report the affected set by 7x — this analysis builds its own many-to-many map instead.
safetyRules.refusedBranch: p000001:rgn:footer1:self with scope 'routes' covering its WHOLE blast radius is still refused as `global-region-requires-explicit-global` (28.P5.41).
safetyRules.safeBranch: The same footer with scope 'global' is accepted: 84 slot keys, 2 occurrences (desktop + mobile), and effect.siblingRegionIds names the 7 OTHER footer ids (28.P5.42 / 28.P5.43 / 28.P5.44). The engine never pretends one id is the whole footer.
safetyRules.measuredNodePartition: On BOTH real templates the compiler PARTITIONS the covered nodes: 18,458 (page,viewport,node) keys are owned by >= 1 region on linear and ZERO by more than one (68,949 / 0 on stripe). The membership map is still built many-to-many, because nesting is possible and the SLOT layer is genuinely shared.

safetyRules.rule: There is no interaction-graph artifact — the graph is `data-wr-*` props on the runtime IR. `scanInteractionEdges` reads all three target channels: `data-wr-target-node`, `data-wr-obs[].i` (a generated DOM id `wr-<pageId>-<viewport>-<nodeId>`) and `data-wr-obs[].hn` (the mount host). A `data-wr-dyn-id` mount names no static target and travels with its trigger. REFUSED when an ENABLED trigger's target (or mount host) is inside the disabled subtree, and when a target that STARTS HIDDEN loses every trigger that could reveal it.
safetyRules.realCounterexample: linear.app homepage. MEASURED over all 8 pages x 2 viewports: 23 triggers, 39 target edges — 6 same-region, 3 CROSS-region, 14 pointing at a node OUTSIDE every region, 16 dyn-mount with no static target. All THREE cross-region edges converge on n001530 in p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:3, triggered from n000021 (in the GLOBAL region global:rgn:nav1:self, which renders on all 8 routes), n000128 (p000001:rgn:nav2:self) and n001659 (p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:4).
safetyRules.refusedBranch: Disabling p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:3 produces exactly 3 `interaction-cut-target-disabled` refusals, each machine-readable with the trigger node, the trigger's regions, the target node and the channel, and each naming the cascade region that would make it safe (28.P5.34 / 28.P5.35 / 28.P5.36).
safetyRules.cascade: Re-issuing the SAME disable together with the 3 named cascade regions CLEARS every target-disabled cut (28.P5.37) — and then exposes a second hazard the engine refuses rather than waves through: 8 `interaction-cut-target-unreachable` refusals with cascadeAvailable=false, because disabling the global nav orphans one hidden target per page and those targets belong to no region (28.P5.38).
safetyRules.safeBranch: The neighbouring section p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:4 disables cleanly — allowed, zero refusals, 670 nodes and 73 slot keys removed (28.P5.39). Its 2 disabled triggers whose targets SURVIVE are REPORTED as `orphanedTargets`, never silently accepted (28.P5.40).

safetyRules.rule: A region id this template does not have is REFUSED as `unknown-region`; a project with no page-regions artifact refuses EVERY region edit as `regions-not-compiled` rather than silently ignoring it.
safetyRules.evidence: smoke:enablement 28.P5.45 / 28.P5.46; smoke:release 28.P5.68 proves it end to end — a stale region id recorded in authored state is refused at resolve time and disables nothing.

refusalShape: { code, subject, message, requestedRoutes, affectedRoutes, cascadeRegionIds, cascadeAvailable, detail } — cascadeAvailable is explicitly FALSE when no cascade can make the request safe (a target that belongs to no region), so a blind spot blocks instead of decorating.

accountingDispositions.whyNotRemoved: `removed` has exactly one producer (accounting.ts: isEmptyValue(value)) and means AN EMPTY VALUE IN A STILL-RENDERED NODE. Reusing it would make an intentionally emptied headline and a physically deleted section indistinguishable in the one artifact whose whole purpose is that they are distinguishable.
accountingDispositions.denominator: A disabled slot stays IN the in-scope population. `inScopeSlotKeys(unitsFile, disabledSlotKeys)` ADDS keys the unit builder no longer sees (a disabled route leaves the content scope), so a disabled slot moves between disposition buckets and never falls out of the total. The reconciliation block still proves originTotal === dispositionTotal === inScopeSlots.
accountingDispositions.precedence: ENABLEMENT WINS over the value-based classification, but ONLY for a slot this plan actually stops rendering. A disabled slot is not `applied` (nothing renders), not `preserved` (the source default does not render either) and above all not `unresolved` — leaving a deliberately deleted section demanding operator input would block a production build on work the operator already decided against. CORRECTED 2026-08-28 (verifier finding, see `corrections`): the region branch had NO guard, so a slot key that is also bound OUTSIDE the disabled region was marked `disabled-region` while it still shipped. `resolveEnablement` now marks `disabled-region` only when EVERY BINDING of the key is inside a node this plan removes or on a page this plan deletes — the same standard the route branch always held. The sentence above is therefore true of the rows that carry the disposition, and was FALSE of 84 rows before the correction.
accountingDispositions.carrier: content-run manifest `enablement` (optional, absent on every run on disk), written by prepareContentRun. buildSlotAccounting is called from ingestGenerationResult, which sees the manifest and not the release project.
accountingDispositions.measuredEndToEnd: smoke:release 28.P5.72 / 28.P6.31 / 28.P5.73 / 28.P5.74 on the REAL fixture build: every slot in the disabled region is `disabled-region`, at least one slot is `disabled-route`, the account reconciles, and NO disabled slot was folded into `removed`.
accountingDispositions.guard: MEASURED on the real linear template: disabling ONE of the 8 `*:rgn:footer1:self` regions (blast radius /changelog) names 84 `global.footer.*` member slot keys, and all 84 are bound on the other 7 ENABLED routes. Before the correction all 84 became `disabled-region`; after it, 0 do, the survivors are reported in `ResolvedEnablement.warnings`, and the plan still removes the region physically (2 region-root nodes). The guard is not a blanket: with /pricing ALSO disabled, the footer keys bound nowhere the plan still renders do land as `disabled-region` (smoke:enablement 28.P6.45–28.P6.49).

limitations: A region id is namespaced by pageSourceId, so `scope: "global"` means 'everywhere THIS REGION ID exists', not 'everywhere this CONTENT exists'. On linear the footer is 8 distinct ids and disabling one removes the footer from one page. The effect names the other 7 as `siblingRegionIds` so an operator surface can offer the whole set, but the engine does NOT auto-expand to them — that is a UI decision I did not make on the operator's behalf.

Signal (iii) — the (landmark, childPath) signature on >= 2 pages — fires on EVERY region of the four-page smoke-regions fixture, whose pages are structurally near-identical. On such a site no region can be disabled per-route at all. That is the union being deliberately wide; it is measured and printed rather than tuned away.

The interaction cut is only as complete as the OBSERVATION was. 14 of linear's 39 edges and, per the enablement recon, 39 of stripe's 59 point at a node outside every region (usually n000002, the adapted document root). Those are refused with cascadeAvailable=false rather than resolved. Content mounted from a `data-wr-dyn-template` string has NO static region membership at all and cannot be reasoned about by region id.

`interaction-cut-target-unreachable` uses `data-wr-hidden` / `data-wr-reveal` as the 'starts hidden' signal. A target hidden purely by CSS with no such prop is not detected, so that rule is a floor, not a ceiling.

The stripe region measurements come from the 2026-08-18T10-45-40-007Z template (9,529 slots, 1,014 regions), because that is the only stripe template with a page-regions compile on disk. Route -> pageSourceId sharing is identical in the newer templates, so the many-to-one property transfers; the region counts do not.

The end-to-end production proof in smoke:release disables the SMALLEST home-page region with content, not the largest. Reason, measured: the fixture's whole home page is a hero plus a tagline and the hero region owns every element carrying a themed style token, so disabling it makes production QA's `theme-computed-paint` fail honestly ('no probe class found in DOM') and the build is not adopted. That is a property of a 2-route fixture, not of the feature; the large-region removal (670 nodes, 73 slot keys) is proven against the real linear template in smoke:enablement §9 and §11 instead.

REGION OFF IN PREVIEW is proven against the REAL Phase-3 authoring preview by applying the plan to the preview workspace's `app/reconstruction-data` between two sessions (the template app is `dynamic = "force-dynamic"`, so the route table and the page trees are read per request). src/authoring-preview/ was NOT edited — it is another builder's file — so the preview does not yet resolve enablement on its own; a caller must apply the plan to the workspace. That wiring is a named gap, not a claim.

`applyEnablementToApp` deletes an orphaned page TREE from the build copy. It does not attempt to renumber or garbage-collect anything else in the app; unreferenced style tokens for a disabled region remain in the generated stylesheet.

No region enablement has been exercised on the stripe lineage through a real production build — stripe has no accepted release project and a compile of that template was out of budget. The stripe evidence is analysis-only (both branches of the shared-page rule).

CORRECTED: the accounting precedence sentence ('not `preserved` — the source default does not render either') was FALSE for 84 slot keys before 2026-08-28. It is now true of every row that carries `disabled-region`, because the disposition is only assigned when no binding of the key survives the plan. A region-member key that survives elsewhere is reported in `ResolvedEnablement.warnings` and keeps its ordinary disposition — including `unresolved`, which is what put four customer-facing blockers back on the board.

The guard is binding-based. A slot with NO bindings at all is vacuously 'bound nowhere this build still renders' and would be marked `disabled-region`; on the real templates every region-member key is derived from bindings, so the case does not arise, but it is a hole in the reasoning rather than a measured impossibility.

The survivor warning is an operator-facing string on the resolved enablement, not a requirement. An operator who disables one footer id still gets the footer removed from ONE page only; the engine names the 7 sibling ids and now also names the 84 keys that keep rendering, but it still does not auto-expand to the siblings.
